factors.name: Net size
factors.summary: Number of duplicate tasks (0.97), Size (0.97) and Token split (0.95) load almost identically, so these count measures largely track how large a net is in this dataset. Density (-0.58) and Average connector degree (-0.48) load negatively, consistent with density shrinking as nets grow, but both also cross-load on Factor 3. It is the strongest factor, with 37.3% explained variance.

factors.name: Connector degree and connectivity
factors.summary: Maximum connector degree (0.95), Coefficient of network connectivity (0.66) and Average connector degree (0.46) share how many arcs meet at nodes and connectors. Average connector degree cross-loads on Factors 1 and 3, and Coefficient of network connectivity also has moderate loadings on Factor 4 (0.48) and Factor 1 (-0.47). The near-perfect communality of Maximum connector degree is a possible Heywood case, so its loading should be read with care.

factors.name: Connector homogeneity with density
factors.summary: The factor is dominated by a strong negative loading of Connector Heterogeneity (-0.93), so it rises when one connector type dominates. Density (0.61) and Average connector degree (0.58) load positively but are cross-loading measures that also load on Factor 1, and Average connector degree also loads on Factor 2. The factor lies beyond the two suggested by the eigenvalues (third eigenvalue 0.91), so the name is tentative.

factors.name: Separability (weak)
factors.summary: Only Separability (0.63) is assigned, with moderate, unassigned loadings of Coefficient of network connectivity (0.48), Average connector degree (0.41) and Density (0.40). It explains 10.7% of the variance and corresponds to an eigenvalue of 0.71. It is a weak, essentially single-measure factor.

interpretation.overall: Bartlett's test is significant and the overall KMO of 0.75 exceeds the threshold of 0.6, so the data are suitable for a factor analysis. Only two eigenvalues exceed 1 (5.46 and 2.20) and two factors were suggested, yet four varimax-rotated factors were extracted, which together explain 85.2% of the variance. The clearest dimension is net size (Factor 1), followed by connector degree and connectivity (Factor 2). Factors 3 and 4 are weaker and partly rest on cross-loading measures (Density, Average connector degree) or on a single measure (Separability). Connector Mismatch remains unassigned because of its low communality (0.21).
caveats: Four factors were extracted although the eigenvalues suggest two, so Factors 3 and 4 may be over-extraction and are fragile.
Maximum connector degree reaches a communality at the bound of the fit (possible Heywood case), which can distort the solution around Factor 2.
Density and Average connector degree cross-load on several factors and do not belong clearly to any single dimension.
Connector Mismatch is unassigned (communality 0.21), so connector imbalance is not represented by any factor.
Sequentiality and Control flow complexity were removed by the MSA filter, and Number of empty sequence flows was constant, so these aspects are absent from the solution.

The near-identical loadings of Size, Number of duplicate tasks and Token split may reflect how the discovery algorithms in this dataset build nets, for example by adding silent transitions, rather than a general property of process models.
The factors describe variance shared in these 288 nets under varimax rotation and may change with other data, rotations or factor counts.
